page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn9ge.64xlarge is a high-density accelerator server instance built on the x86_64 architecture for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Powered by AMD EPYC 9A75 processors operating at 3.3 GHz, it provides 256 dedicated vCPUs alongside 2304 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 9.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server integrates 8 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs with a combined total of 576 GB of GPU VRAM.

The instance incorporates a high-bandwidth network architecture with 380 Gbps of baseline network throughput. Local NVMe or SSD storage is not included with this instance type, requiring all storage traffic to route to external network-attached block storage devices. The hardware profile balances raw parallel processing power from eight dedicated hardware accelerators with heavy network throughput, though non-volatile persistent storage relies on external network storage latency.

Given its cluster network connectivity, massive system memory, and 8 discrete NVIDIA Blackwell accelerators, this instance delivers high qualitative resource density for parallel compute tasks. It is configured for large language model training, distributed deep learning, complex generative AI models, high-performance computing simulations, and multi-node machine learning pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmgn9ge.64xlarge is a specialized high-performance cloud instance optimized for heavy artificial intelligence and compute workloads. The server features 8 integrated NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs with a total of 576 GB of VRAM, supported by a 380 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Local disk storage is not bundled, necessitating external network-attached storage solutions for persistence. The high accelerator density and vast GPU memory pool offer substantial processing capacity for resource-intensive tasks, balancing raw hardware density with cluster networking capability. This server is suited for large language model inference and training, high-performance computing simulations, distributed machine learning pipelines, and massive data analytics workloads requiring parallel accelerator performance.
